newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end lower in mixed, choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end lower in mixed, choppy trade.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed lower on Thursday in busy and sometimes erratic trade boosted by put-throughs, with sharp losses again in Gas Natural contrasting with strength in key stocks.
The general index fell 0.96 points, 0.27 percent, to 348.36 and the Ibex shed 12.89 points, 0.32 percent, to 3,953.33.
Gas Natural took another big loss, ending down 1,540 pesetas at 20,040 as traders focussed on the implications of the end of a period of "protection" by the government.
Repsol, holder of Gas Natural majority stake, was resilient nevertheless. It rose 20 pesetas to 4,055.
The gas firm's losses were based on a lower-than-expected rise in the gas tariff. But the implications are wider.
"Up to now (Gas Natural's) profile was one of strong growth with fat margins, a company which the government favoured and a safe stock. Now that perception has changed," said an analyst.
This may mean all officially-regulated firms may be due for the same treatment, and sentiment has taken a blow, they said.
"There's no will to buy and the market is not strong, so its more likely for us to carry on down in the next few days," a trader said.
